title: The locus where the fibre dimension of a finite type ring map is at most d is a neighbourhood of a point where it equals d
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q'\subset S$ with $\mathfrak p'=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$, let $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ be the residue fields, $F_{\mathfrak p'}=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak Q'\subset F_{\mathfrak p'}$ the kernel of the ring map $F_{\mathfrak p'}\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (a prime ideal), and let $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak p'}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak Q'$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Let $d\ge0$ be an integer and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal with $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)=d$. Then there is an open subset $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ (Zariski topology) with $\mathfrak q\in V$ such that $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)\le d$ for every prime $\mathfrak q'\in V$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, line 31308) and its proof (via Lemma Tag 00QE, lemma-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, and Lemma Tag 00QG, lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra); dim_q(S/R) is Definition Tag 00QD (definition-relative-dimension, line 31150); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra] to $R\to S$, $\mathfrak q$, and $n=d$. Choose $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and an $R$-algebra map $P=R[t_1,\dots,t_d]\to S_g$ quasi-finite at every prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], $V=D(g)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$; every $\mathfrak q'\in V$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q'_g$ of $S_g$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, lines 31317-31320): reduction by Lemma Tag 00QE (lemma-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra)

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q'\in D(g)$ and put $\mathfrak p'=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$. Put $T=S_g\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. The isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] identifies $T$ with $S_g\otimes_S(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p'))$; then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] identifies it with $F_{\mathfrak p',\bar g}$, the localization of $F_{\mathfrak p'}=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ at $\bar g$. The base change of $P$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_d]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], and its map to $T$ is the base change of $P\to S_g$, by the same tensor-cancellation isomorphism with $S=P$. The latter is quasi-finite at every prime, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings], with $R=P$, $S=S_g$, $R'=\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_d]$ and $S'=T$, shows that the polynomial-to-$T$ map is quasi-finite at every prime (the tensor map to $T$ is an isomorphism and hence surjective). It is of finite type because the finitely many $R$-algebra generators of $S$, together with $g^{-1}$, generate $T$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_d]$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, lines 31319-31322), 'Considering the fibres'; quasi-finite base change is Lemma Tag 00PP (lemma-quasi-finite-base-change, lines 30362-30388), through the existing four-rings form Tag 00PN

proof.text: Since $T$ is a finite type $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra with a quasi-finite map from $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_d]$, [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra] gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T\le d$. Thus the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at any of its points is at most $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions]. In particular this holds at the point $\mathfrak Q'_g$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q'_g$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, lines 31320-31322), via Lemma Tag 00QG (lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra); local dimension bound from Topology Tag 0B7I

proof.text: Under $T\cong F_{\mathfrak p',\bar g}$ from step 2, $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is the open subspace $D(\bar g)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak p'}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. The fibre-prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] identifies $\mathfrak Q'_g$ with the prime $\mathfrak Q'$ associated to $\mathfrak q'$; it lies in $D(\bar g)$ because $g\notin\mathfrak q'$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] gives $\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak p'}=\dim_{\mathfrak Q'_g}\operatorname{Spec}T\le d$ by step 3. This is $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)\le d$, for every $\mathfrak q'\in V$.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks 00QH along its source proof: 00QE supplies a principal neighbourhood with a quasi-finite map from an n-variable polynomial ring; the existing four-rings lemma passes quasi-finiteness to every residue-field fibre; 00QG bounds the dimension of each such fibre; and localization plus invariance of local dimension on an open subspace gives the bound at every prime in the neighbourhood.
